II. MACROECONOMIC POLICY FRAMEWORK

Despite the political uncertainty that prevailed following the end of the civil

23.

war in 2006, there has broadly been consensus on economic policy. While significant

political differences across and within political parties have prevented progress on key

constitutional issues, there has been broad - albeit informal - consensus around economic

policies and priorities. This has allowed progress on a range of technical issues including

public financial management, monetary policy, and financial sector supervision.
